title: Finite smooth orientation, adjunction and reduction data
statement: Let A be a finite commutative ring annihilated by N>0, f:X→Y a compactifiable separated quasi-compact morphism of Noetherian schemes and d≥0. Use the actual ordinary and pro-etale sources, exceptional functors, intrinsic Ctf predicate, normalized diagonal orientation and counits of [def-pur-finite-smooth-canonical-maps]. Define SmoothLevel to be data consisting of the actual diagonal Rees geometry of [def-pur-finite-ring-section-data], invertibility of N on X, and an orientation alpha with that normalization, together with the following properties: the ordinary gamma is invertible on bounded constructible finite-Tor inputs and natural on all ordinary inputs; Rnu_* carries every intrinsic Ctf input on Y to ordinary bounded constructible finite-Tor and its actual comparison counit is invertible; pro-etale gamma is an isomorphism, natural on Ctf, and its source and target are Ctf; the specified formula and the trace transport hold for every ordinary origin and every isomorphism from that origin to the given intrinsic input. In dimension zero, require existence of the graph-normalized compact-support/sum comparisons of [def-pur-finite-smooth-comparison-coordinates], and for every normalized comparison require gamma to identify with the actual etale adjunction coordinates and trace with the actual etale-sum counit. Require the coefficient unit and its gamma source and target to be Ctf, and the latter two to have no cohomology outside degree -2d. For phi:A→B and two such levels, define ReductionData using the normalized root-line and scalar comparisons of [def-pur-finite-smooth-coefficient-arrows]: ordinary and pro-etale compact-support comparisons are invertible on Ctf; exceptional comparisons are invertible and satisfy the actual counit-transpose identity; S(gamma_A) followed by c equals lambda followed by gamma_B; derived scalar extension preserves intrinsic Ctf; the pro-etale exceptional comparison is natural and the pullback and lambda comparisons are invertible on Ctf. The equations at dimension zero include the canonical identification of the zero-fold line with the coefficient unit. Level(ell,n) abbreviates this structure for A=Z/(ell^n), N=ell^n. These are definitions of data and properties, not assumptions of their existence.

source.place: sk-thm-smooth-purity and proof: inverse diagonal orientation followed by the tensor map; sk-prop-sp-orientation.proof.md: diagonal, deformation, vector bundle; sk-lem-sp-reduction.proof.md and sk-lem-sp-reduction-compatibilities.proof.md: counit-defined coefficient comparisons and quotient cocycle. The ordinary-etale Noetherian formulation retains arbitrary ground fields.
